About

Careful work, shipped to production.

I've spent four years inside ERPNext and the Frappe Framework, first at Cloud Hire and now at Websar IT Solutions, working with clinics, pharmacies, online stores and, more recently, manufacturers whose sales and production run through the system every hour of the day.

My approach is simple: understand the actual workflow before touching a DocType, build things as installable apps rather than one-off patches, and stay around after go-live to make sure they hold up.

Healthcare, e-commerce and manufacturing are where I have shipped so far, but the work underneath is the same in every business: master data, transactions, approvals, reports and integrations. If your process can be drawn on a whiteboard, it can be built in ERPNext — whatever the industry or module.

Understand first. Build once. Keep it running.

Built as installable apps

Modules running in production today.

Each one is a packaged Frappe app with its own DocTypes, hooks and scheduled jobs — not a pile of one-off customisations.

Healthcare · Frappe Cloud · installable app

Pharmacy inventory & alerts

Replaced spreadsheet-based pharmacy stock tracking inside a clinic's ERPNext.

  • Stock intake, batch-wise tracking, warehouse transfers and adjustments
  • Low-stock alerts by email and WhatsApp the moment an item crosses its re-order level
  • Expiry warnings at 30, 15 and 7 days to reduce expired-medicine write-offs
  • Inventory dashboard and Current Stock Report with number cards and filters
Healthcare · Frappe Cloud · installable app

Teleconsultation inside ERPNext

Video consultations run end-to-end from the Patient Appointment, with nothing shared by hand.

  • Google Meet link generated on booking, sent to doctor and patient by email and WhatsApp
  • Reminder engine on a 30-minute scheduled job, sending reminders about an hour before each consultation
  • Reports for doctor-wise load, encounter history and follow-ups due
  • Central Settings DocType with configurable WhatsApp templates
Manufacturing · Frappe Cloud · GitHub deploy

Order-to-cash for an engineering manufacturer

A sales operating system for a manufacturer handling large, document-heavy industrial orders.

  • Enquiry and quotation register with item rows, competitor pricing and won/lost reasons
  • Cost sheets built from raw-material groups and product masters, with cost history
  • Security-deposit / bank-guarantee tracker with expiry and refund follow-up
  • Document tracker for NDA, drawing approval, QAP, inspection plans and RM reports, with generated documents from standard templates
  • Payment tracker activated on invoicing, plus ageing, overdue and pending-document reports
Manufacturing · Frappe Cloud · no-terminal deployment

Multi-stage production for a jari (zari) manufacturer

Core and production apps for silver-based yarn that passes through melting, wire-drawing, pavtha, taniya and spindle stages with outside job-workers.

  • Issue and receive documents at every stage, with a single inventory ledger behind them
  • Silver purity and weight-based accounting, normalised units, loss standards per process
  • Job-worker payout formats that compute payment, loss and waste on receipt
  • Product, quality, process, worker, department and machine masters
  • Repairs and clean-ups delivered safely via System Console scripts within safe_exec restrictions
UI theme

A calmer ERPNext for long shifts.

A healthcare operations team was reading a flat white page with grey boxes for most of the day. I designed a complete theme for ERPNext Desk and delivered it as CSS only: a dark frame around the app, a bright, easy-to-read work area, and a single teal highlight used only to show where you are on the screen.

Every colour is named and documented, every part of the ERPNext screen is mapped to it, and every text-and-background combination was checked against the WCAG 2.1 accessibility standard in both light and dark mode. ERPNext’s core files are untouched, so the theme survives Frappe upgrades.
